candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.7, Management of Care — concepts of management, supervision, safe care delivery, and organizational responsibilities
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — unit orientation and staff competence
candidate.educational_objective: Describe orientation as role- and setting-specific initial training, safety preparation, and competence assessment for staff entering a new clinical environment.

options.A: Provide initial training and information about the organization, role, policies, essential job functions, and key safety content while assessing competence for assigned responsibilities.
options.B: Replace professional nursing education and licensure with facility-specific employment training and policies.
options.C: Apply only to newly graduated nurses because experienced nurses do not need orientation when entering a different clinical setting.
options.D: Require a fixed orientation period for every nurse even after the organization has determined that the nurse is competent for the assigned responsibilities.

candidate.rationale: The Joint Commission defines orientation as providing initial training and information while assessing clinical staff competence relative to job responsibilities and organizational mission and goals. Orientation includes adjustment to the new setting, policies/procedures, essential job functions, and key safety content. Its duration is determined by the organization and the complexity of the required competencies rather than a universal fixed period. A is correct; B, C, and D conflict with these standards.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Orientation provides initial training/information and assesses competence relative to job duties and organizational expectations, includes key safety content, and does not require a universal fixed duration.
candidate.source_document_title: Standards FAQ — Competency Assessment vs Orientation
candidate.source_locator: Orientation definition; description of introductory program/activities; HR.01.04.01 examples of Key Safety Content; discussion of organization-determined duration and competency requirements
